cause.summary: Every log-binomial fit of ours converges, plain or COPY, so ours counts 48 of 48 non-linear scenarios against the paper's 30. The paper's failures are failures of SAS GENMOD's optimizer on the COPY data, which we cannot run. The boundary that COPY handles is common in our non-linear runs: COPY is needed in some fit of {copy_non} of 48 non-linear scenarios (up to {copy_non_max} of 1,000 fits, median {copy_non_med}) and of {copy_lin} of 48 linear ones (at most {copy_lin_max} fits), which agrees with the paper's split between the forms but cannot say which 18 failed.

cause.summary: The simulation program was never released, and the revised COPY macro of Petersen and Deddens is not online (its NIOSH page answers 403). Both are SAS, which no free runtime runs. The method is implemented from the paper's text and checked against its printed tables.

simulation.what: Contamination flips the outcome of the records whose true p_y lies beyond the population's rate/2 and 1 - rate/2 quantiles of p_y (computed exactly for each scenario), so the number flipped varies between data sets ({flip5_mean} on average at 5% and n = 1500, SD {flip5_sd}). The paper says only 'p_y at bottom or top 1%' (2.5% for 5%)
simulation.sensitivity: Two readings tested on every contaminated cell. Flipping exactly ceil(n rate/2) records per tail in every data set ({flip5_sample} at 5%, n = 1500) leaves the means where they are (Table 1 {h_sample_table1} of {h_sample_table1_of} within tolerance) but makes the SEs too small at outcome 10% and 5% contamination: Table 2 {h_sample_table2}, Table A1 {h_sample500_tableA1}, Table A2 {h_sample500_tableA2} of 96 contaminated cells within tolerance, against {h_sample_table2_main}, {h_sample500_tableA1_main} and {h_sample500_tableA2_main} with population cut-offs.

simulation.what: Both tails are flipped (2%: the bottom 1% and the top 1% of p_y)
simulation.sensitivity: The whole rate flipped at the bottom gives {h_bottom_table1} of 96 contaminated cells of Table 1 within tolerance, at the top {h_top_table1}; both tails {h_bottom_table1_main}.

simulation.what: Records are ranked by the true p_y of the generating model
simulation.sensitivity: Ranking by p_y fitted by the uncontaminated log-binomial model (a fixed number per data set) gives {h_fitted_table1} of 96 contaminated cells of Table 1 within tolerance and {h_fitted_table3} of Table 3.

simulation.what: The fitted models include Z^2 when the confounder is quadratic (the Discussion speaks of 'the higher-order term of Z' added into the model; the Methods do not say)
simulation.sensitivity: Leaving Z^2 out gives {h_noquad_table1} of {h_noquad_table1_of} non-linear cells of Table 1 within tolerance and {h_noquad_table3} of Table 3, against {h_noquad_table1_main} and {h_noquad_table3_main} with it.

simulation.what: The log-binomial fit reported is the maximum likelihood fit when it lies inside the parameter space, else the COPY fit with C = 1,000,000 (weights C on the data, 1 on the data with the outcome reversed); our solver is Newton's method with a line search, not SAS GENMOD
simulation.sensitivity: When the maximum is interior the COPY fit equals it to O(1/C), so the switching rule does not move the estimates. Our fits equal an independent maximizer's: {x_detail}.

simulation.what: Random numbers: NumPy's PCG64 with fixed seeds per scenario; the paper's SAS seeds are not given
simulation.sensitivity: A second run with other seeds puts {second_within} of {cells} printed cells within tolerance.

simulation.what: The alpha0 and beta0 of Additional file 1 are used for n = 500 too
simulation.sensitivity: Not varied; Tables A1-A3 come back at {tableA1_within}, {tableA2_within} and {tableA3_within} of 144 cells.

simulation.what: The empirical SE uses the divisor 999 and the MSE is the squared mean error plus that variance
simulation.sensitivity: The divisor 1,000 changes an SE by 0.05% of its value, far below the printed precision.

page.lede: Chen, Shi, Qian and Azen asked which model for relative risks holds up when a few outcomes are recorded wrong. Their SAS program was never released. We rebuilt the simulation from the paper and ran all 24 scenarios again. {within} of {cells} printed table cells came back within Monte Carlo error.

page.grid_caption: Paper above, ours below; shaded where ours is outside the Monte Carlo tolerance.
page.slip_note: The italic cell is a misprint of the paper and is left out.
page.tables_caption: Every printed cell of Tables 1 to 3 (n = 1500) and of Tables A1 to A3 in Additional file 2 (n = 500), in the paper's layout. A cell agrees when ours is within half a printed unit plus three times the Monte Carlo error of the difference of two {reps} replicate estimates.
page.items_caption: Each table, figure panel and statement of the paper. check_results.py computes every verdict from the numbers.
page.claims_line: The main claim {main_verdict}. Every claim about bias, SE and MSE holds on our run. The one table cell that misses is a misprint in Table 3, and the convergence count of the Discussion belongs to SAS, which we cannot run.
came_back: All 24 scenarios at n = 1500 and n = 500, rebuilt as the Python package robustrr and run again with {reps} replicates each.
{within} of {cells} printed cells within Monte Carlo error. The one miss is Table 3 printing 0.013 where its own bias and SE give {typo_implied}; ours is {typo_ours}.
Records past fixed quantiles of p_y are flipped, so how many are flipped varies from data set to data set. Flipping a fixed number in every data set makes the SEs too small at outcome 10%.
Drawn on the published picture. Panel A passes the 2 px test. B, C and D sit within Monte Carlo noise of the published lines, which a 2 px test cannot resolve.
Robust Poisson is less biased than log-binomial in every contaminated cell with a quadratic confounder, and the two are close with a linear one.
buried: The authors' SAS 9.2 program and the revised COPY macro.
Which 18 non-linear scenarios SAS failed to fit. Every fit of ours converges.
